title: Unlocking Zero-Shot Geospatial Reasoning via Indirect Rewards
claim: Our method beats the baseline and ablated variants across nearly every task in a zero-shot comparison.
layout: single radar chart, 13 task axes, color-grouped by category, legend top-right
description: A single large radar (spider) chart with 13 spokes labeled Task0 to Task12. The labels are colored by category: blue for Geographical, green for Environmental, brown for Sociocultural and purple for Geolocation. Matching pale background wedges mark each category, and a category legend sits at lower right. Dashed concentric rings are labeled 20%, 40%, 60% and 80%. Four filled polygons are overlaid. They are Qwen2.5-VL-7B in teal, Geo-SFT in light green, Geo-R1-Zero in orange and Geo-R1 in thick dark magenta, with the legend at top right. The magenta Geo-R1 outline encloses the others on almost every axis and reaches the outer ring on several tasks. The baselines collapse toward the center on Task8 through Task12.
caption: Geo-R1 significantly outperforms baseline [ref] across 13 verifiable geo-reasoning tasks on the GeoChain benchmark [ref] in the zero-shot setting. See Table [ref] for detailed description of these tasks.
abstract: Training robust reasoning vision-language models (VLMs) in rare domains (such as geospatial) is fundamentally constrained by supervision scarcity. While raw geospatial imagery is abundant, the amount of task-direct supervision falls far behind that of common domains. In this work, we validate an important conclusion: indirect verifiable rewards, derived from seemingly unrelated metadata, are sufficient to induce sophisticated and generalizable geospatial reasoning across a wide range of downstream tasks (25+). We present Geo-R1 as one empirical instantiation of this paradigm. Rather than relying on limited task-specific annotations (i.e., direct rewards), Geo-R1 utilizes scalable, verifiable indirect proxy rewards based on cross-view alignment with metadata (geolocation information) to drive reinforcement learning at scale. Such indirect rewards successfully motivate the model to discover and internalize zero-shot geospatial reasoning across diverse tasks, achieving extraordinary zero-shot transfer on out-of-distribution benchmarks and even surpassing fully supervised specialists on certain benchmarks. These findings indicate that optimizing for indirect verifiable rewards may provide a scalable pathway to unlock generalized reasoning capabilities in rare domains with massive unlabeled data archives. Our code is availavle at: https://github.com/miniHuiHui/Geo-R1.
